apps.name: Altitude Unknown RC Configurator
apps.summary: Set up transmitter models and instructor/student options, and update firmware on the transmitter, the receiver, and the ASCEND flight controller.

apps.name: ASCEND Flight Control
apps.summary: The ground station made for the ASCEND flight controller: plan and upload missions on a map with the VFR sectional chart and FAA airspace layers (TFRs, UAS Facility Maps, controlled airspace), lay out survey grids that take photos by distance, watch a flight with an attitude indicator and the airplane's track, change settings explained in plain English, and run the accelerometer, level, compass, and radio calibrations. The RC Configurator is built in.
apps.pinnedRelease: RC-Airplane's latest release must stay the RC Configurator (its firmware updater reads it), so this links to a specific ASCEND Flight Control release. Update it with each new release.
apps.note: Beta: tested with the ArduPilot simulator but not yet on many airplanes, so save a backup of your settings first (Aircraft Settings, then Save Backup…). On Windows, if you see “Windows protected your PC,” choose More info, then Run anyway.

apps.name: Flight Lab RC
apps.summary: A free RC flight simulator with flying sites, wind, and thermals. Practice with the Altitude Unknown transmitter or a gamepad before flying the trainer.
apps.note: Derived from PicaSim; free for noncommercial use.

apps.name: QGroundControl
apps.summary: Connect to the ASCEND flight controller to check sensors, calibrate, change ArduPilot parameters, and plan autonomous missions.
apps.note: Made by the Dronecode project, not Altitude Unknown. The download link opens the official QGroundControl install page. Don't use its Firmware page on the ASCEND flight controller: update firmware only with the RC Configurator.

apps.name: Mission Planner
apps.summary: An alternative to QGroundControl for the ASCEND flight controller: calibrate, change ArduPilot parameters, view telemetry, and plan autonomous missions. Use whichever your team prefers.
apps.note: Made by the ArduPilot project, not Altitude Unknown. The download link opens the official Mission Planner page. Windows only; Mac teams use QGroundControl. Don't use its Install Firmware page on the ASCEND flight controller: update firmware only with the RC Configurator.

apps.name: YELLOWSTONE Ground Station
apps.summary: The ground station for YELLOWSTONE, the balloon tracking and flight termination board, which balloon teams use to follow their flight.

apps.name: Flight KML Sectional Overlay
apps.summary: Draw a balloon flight prediction (KML) on an FAA VFR sectional chart and export the map as PNG or PDF for FAA submissions.

apps.name: ASCEND Logger
apps.summary: Records GPS position and time, pressure, and particulate readings to a microSD card as CSV that follows the ASCEND data standard. The repository holds the logger firmware, bench tools, and the schematic and board files.
apps.note: Firmware downloads will be added when the logger firmware is released. The source and board design are available now.

apps.name: SAMD21 Bootloader Flasher
apps.summary: Install the Altitude Unknown USB bootloader on new SAMD21 boards (transmitter, receiver, YELLOWSTONE, and BOREALIS) with an Atmel-ICE programmer. Check Board shows which chip and bootloader a board has; Install Bootloader writes, verifies, and protects it. The bootloader lets the board take Arduino uploads over USB and shows a drive you can drop a UF2 file on.
apps.note: Most teams never need this: boards arrive with their bootloader installed. The bootloader itself is open source too: Altitude-Unknown/Altitude-SAMD21-Bootloader on GitHub.
